body:
## What

- version individual tiles instead of invalidating every tile after a chunk update
- cache versioned existing tiles for one year as `immutable`, while preserving ETag revalidation for unversioned requests and `no-store` for missing tiles
- constrain each dimension to its metadata bounds with a 16-block margin
- add a Leaflet-style home control that restores the calculated initial center and zoom for the active dimension

Legacy `tiles_ready` messages that only contain chunk coordinates remain supported: the client conservatively versions every intersecting tile using the message timestamp.

## Why

The previous global tile version changed every tile URL whenever any chunk was updated. Returning to an already visited area therefore downloaded unchanged tiles again. The map also allowed unlimited panning outside explored metadata bounds and had no way to recover the original view after a long pan or zoom sequence.

## Cache behavior

- existing tile with `?v=`: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`
- existing tile without a version: ETag revalidation with the existing cache policy
- missing tile: `Cache-Control: no-store`

## Bounds and reset behavior

Bounds are recalculated from the active dimension metadata whenever metadata or the dimension changes. They use fully sticky Leaflet bounds and add 16 blocks on every side. The home control appears above zoom and restores the stored initial center and zoom for the current dimension.

## Tests

- server: 9 passed
- web unit: 15 passed
- web typecheck and production build: passed
- Playwright: 8 passed

The tests cover stable URLs for unchanged tiles, targeted version changes, all three cache response modes, dimension-specific bounds, and exact initial-view restoration.

author: jlaine
body:
When parsing an SCTP packet:

- Ensure it is long enough to accomodate at least the common header and one chunk's header : 16 bytes.
- Ensure chunks never have a length less than 4 bytes. Otherwise a malformed chunk could cause the parser to loop forever.
- Ensure a chunk's length does not exceed the remaining packet data.

Thanks to Brian Lee from the Systems Software & Security Lab at Georgia Tech for reporting the case of a zero length DATA chunk.

body:
## Summary

The Performance-tab **Duration** chart in the monitor detail flyout (overview page) used a hard-coded `now-12h` window regardless of when the monitor was created. For monitors younger than that window, most date-histogram buckets are empty, so each series collapses to a single data point — rendered by Elastic Charts as a **dot instead of a line** — and the chart's auto y-axis scaling ends up excluding the data, leaving the chart looking empty.

This mirrors the behavior the working monitor **details page** avoids: it anchors its lower time bound to the monitor's `created_at` (via `useMonitorRangeFrom`) rather than a fixed relative window.

### Fix

- Introduce `getDurationChartTimeRange(createdAt)` which, when the monitor is younger than the 12h look-back window, anchors the chart's lower bound at the monitor's creation time.
- In that case, drop the previous-period comparison series (there is no full prior window to compare against), which also removes the `area` + `timeShift` multi-series combination that confused auto y-axis scaling.
- Monitors older than the window (and remote monitors, which have no local `created_at`) keep the existing `now-12h` behavior with the current-vs-previous comparison.

Closes #221399

## Test plan

- [ ] Create a monitor and immediately open its flyout → **Performance** tab. The Duration chart renders a line (not an empty chart / lone dot) from creation time to now.
- [ ] Toggle **All locations** on a multi-location monitor → each location renders a line.
- [ ] Open the flyout for a monitor older than 12h → chart still shows the current-vs-"Previous period" comparison over the 12h window.
- [ ] Remote (CCS) monitor flyout → unchanged behavior.
- [ ] Unit tests: `node scripts/jest x-pack/solutions/observability/plugins/synthetics/public/apps/synthetics/components/monitors_page/overview/overview/monitor_detail_flyout.test.tsx`

## Summary
- **서버 cron self-heal (핵심)**: 신규 cron `/api/cron/topline-resume-sweep` (`* * * * *`, `Bearer CRON_SECRET`). `updated_at` 이 90s 넘게 정체된 `status='generating'` 탑라인을 백그라운드에서 재점화 — **client GET 무관**. 재점화는 GET on-read 경로와 **동일한** `selfHealStaleTopline` 재사용이라 `resume_count` bump·`MAX_RESUME_HOPS=30` 가드·홉 소진 시 error 종결이 그대로 적용(멱등/스키마 불변). 이로써 self-heal 이 **6분·client-GET 의존 → 90s·서버 자동** 으로 단축돼 페이지를 닫아도 완주.
- **map catch logError (#469 관측)**: primary 체인 파단 사유를 error_events/이메일 digest 에 노출 — `topline_map_call_failed`(하드 장애=error / 2-attempt 소진 일시장애=warn), `topline_kick_failed`(kickResume self-fetch 소진=warn), `topline_hop_walltime`(230s 벽 도달 map 미완 홉 hand-off=warn). "primary 체인이 왜 ~15-20 docs 마다 끊기나" 가 다음번엔 데이터로 뜸.
- 멱등/스키마 불변, 회귀 0, 마이그 없음. #1014(GET self-heal)·#1015(logError) 위 확장.

## 진단 근거 (prod, 2026-07-13, #1014 배포 후)
60-doc 탑라인이 수동 재생성 없이 자동 완주(`resume_count=3, done`)했으나 총 28분. 병목 = self-heal 6분 창 + client-GET 의존 + primary 체인이 ~15-20 docs 마다 끊기는 미포착 사유.

## 보수적 해석 명시
- spec 2)의 `topline_hop_walltime` 은 "함수 벽 도달" 예시 코드 — 정상 흐름(대형 프로젝트의 walltime 홉 hand-off)이므로 `severity='warn'` + **고정 message** 로 signature dedup 하여 홉마다의 반복을 한 시그니처로 collapse(flood 방지), count 로 cadence 추세만 드러냄.
- spec 3) `kickResume` 재시도 견고화는 #468 에서 이미 구현됨(`KICK_RESUME_ATTEMPTS=3` + 백오프). 본 PR 은 그 위에 관측(`topline_kick_failed`)만 보강.
- cron staleness 90s 는 *cutoff*, Vercel cron 최소 granularity 는 1분이라 schedule 은 `* * * * *`. 재점화 시 `resume_count` bump → `updated_at` 갱신 → 같은 row 는 다음 90s 전까지 재대상 제외 = 창당 최대 1회로 kick 폭주 자연 바운드.

## Test plan
- [ ] 로컬 lint/typecheck 통과 (build 는 Vercel preview 가 검증 — 로컬 next build 스킵) ✅ 0 errors
- [ ] Vercel preview: 60-doc 탑라인 생성 → **페이지 닫아도** 백그라운드 cron 이 재kick → 완주. 총 소요 28분 대비 단축(stall 당 6분→~90-150s).
- [ ] 정상 진행 중 탑라인은 cron 이 안 건드림(살아 있는 홉은 heartbeat 로 90s 창 안 넘김).

- [ ] MAX_RESUME_HOPS 초과 시 cron 이 진행도 포함 error 종결(무한 방지).

- **cron 등록 확인**: Vercel → Project → Settings → Cron Jobs 에 `topline-resume-sweep` (`* * * * *`) 노출.
- **DB (재점화 발화)**: 새 60-doc 탑라인 생성 후 페이지 닫기 → `select status, map_done, map_total, resume_count, updated_at from interview_toplines where id='<id>'` 로 `resume_count` 가 백그라운드에서 오르며 `done` 도달 확인.

body:
## Summary

Records how much of our token budget we consume whenever Claude runs on the station — **fully local, usage numbers only** (never prompts, cwd, or transcript paths), sliceable **per session / project / agent**, for later plots and burn-rate analysis.

Closes #82

## How it works

- **Source = the Claude Code statusline stdin payload**, which carries per-session `context_window.*` (context fill) *and* account-level `rate_limits.{five_hour,seven_day}.{used_percentage,resets_at}` (authoritative 5h/weekly %, Max only, after the first response). Hooks don't carry usage; browser-cookie polling doesn't apply to a CLI daemon. JSONL transcripts give authoritative per-turn token counts as a complementary/backfill source.
- **`reck-statusline.sh` forwarder** (twin of the existing hook shim): inherits the per-pane `RECK_*` env, fail-closes without it, HMAC-signs, backgrounds the POST. Installed as the Claude `statusLine` while **preserving/chaining/restoring** any prior user statusline.
- **`POST /panes/{id}/usage-sample`** reuses the per-pane HMAC auth (bearer-exempt, exactly like `agent-event`).
- **`daemon/internal/usage/`**: SQLite store (`modernc.org/sqlite`, pure Go / no cgo) at `~/.config/reck/usage/usage.db`.

## Write model (idle filtered out)

Purely **event-driven, write-on-change**, rate-capped to ~1/min per session with an immediate write on a large jump. **Idle panes write nothing** — liveness is a bounded `agent_sessions.last_seen` upsert, not a per-minute row. Account-level quota is **coalesced into one series** across concurrent agents. DB growth is proportional to activity, not to how long panes stay open.

## Tables

`context_samples`, `quota_samples`, `turn_usage` (per-turn from JSONL, deduped by `message_id`), `agent_sessions`, `schema_meta` (holds an `install_id` reserved for a future opt-in anonymous uplink).

## UI (deliberately minimal)

A dim `ctx 43% · 5h 61%` badge on Claude tabs, fed by a paneId→usage map (no change to the persisted layout). It's a snapshot taken at project open. **A proper usage-viewing UI is a separate later pass.** Read routes `GET /usage/summary` and `GET /usage/series?kind=context|quota` are the foundation for that and for a future Chrome-extension cross-check.

## Review

Went through a 3-reviewer pass (security, Go, TypeScript). **No CRITICAL/HIGH, no security issues, no secrets.** Follow-up commit addressed the MEDIUM correctness findings: don't lose a sample on insert error (keep it pending), close the DB only after HTTP/WS drain, and stop an oversized-JSONL-line infinite re-scan. Plus proto.md docs, a `formatPaneUsage` unit test, and a `safeSessionID` path guard.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` (daemon) — all packages pass, incl. new unit/integration tests for store, change-gate (rate-cap/idle/jump/quota-coalescing), backfill dedup + oversized-line + unsafe-id guard, insert-error retry, installer statusLine wire/restore, signed endpoint ingest, and read routes.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` + `formatPaneUsage` vitest pass. (Pre-existing `rsync-copy`/`project-push` station-root test failures are unrelated to this change.)
- [ ] **Station E2E (reviewer to run):** spawn a Claude pane on the station, send messages, then `sqlite3 ~/.config/reck/usage/usage.db 'select * from context_samples order by ts desc limit 5; select * from quota_samples order by ts desc limit 3;'` — context fill climbs and 5h/weekly % appear (Max plan). Two concurrent Claude panes → distinct `context_samples` attribution, one coalesced `quota_samples` series.

## Follow-up to #22 (post-merge fixes)

PR #22 merged an earlier snapshot of this branch. These 4 commits were pushed
afterward and never reached `main`, so `main` still has the bugs below. Same
branch, clean diff against `main` (5 files).

## Bug fixes

- **Reject off-plot GPS outliers before the fit** (`filterPlotOutliers`) — the
  backfill surfaced ~52 off-site photos (up to 6.9 km away). A single km-scale
  outlier dominates the least-squares affine fit. Pure helper + tests, applied
  in `fit-georeference.mjs`.
- **Exclude rejected photos from control points** — `reject` sets
  `review_status='rejected'` but leaves `zone_id` pointing at the zone the photo
  does NOT belong to. The fit query keyed only on `reviewed_at`, turning 8
  rejected rows into false GPS→zone correspondences. Now filters
  `review_status='confirmed'`.
- **Paginate the area-rerun** — supabase-js caps a select at 1000 rows; with
  ~2822 unreviewed geotagged photos the rerun silently skipped ~1800. Now pages
  through all rows.

## Docs

body:
## What & why

TypeScript 7 (the native/`tsgo` compiler) is now testable on npm (`@typescript/native-preview`, and `typescript@7.x`). I checked whether this repo is ready for it and fixed the small number of things that only work due to TS6-specific behavior. These changes are all **safe on the current TS6 toolchain** — nothing is deferred to a future TS bump.

With these three changes, the full dev monorepo builds under **both** the current `tsc` (TS6) **and** the TS7 native compiler with **0 errors**.

## Changes

**1. `tsconfig.json` — `baseUrl` removed in TS7**
TS7 removed the `baseUrl` compiler option (`TS5102`), and its non-relative `paths` values then fail with `TS5090`. The root config used `baseUrl: "packages"` with non-relative mappings (TS6 only tolerated this via `ignoreDeprecations: "6.0"`).
- Dropped `baseUrl`.
- Rewrote all 67 `paths` values to be repo-root-relative (`./packages/...`) — the same pattern `tsconfig.build.json` already uses. Every mapping resolves to the exact same location as before.

**2. `vitest.config.mts` — kept in lockstep**
Vitest derives its resolve aliases from `tsconfig.json`'s `paths` and previously prepended `"packages"` (baking in the old `baseUrl` assumption). Since the paths now already contain `packages/`, the aliases resolve against the repo root directly. Without this the aliases would have doubled to `packages/packages/...` and broken unit tests.

**3. `packages/dev/core/src/Rendering/edgesRenderer.pure.ts` — stricter TS7 inference**
TS7's element-access inference flags `const x1 = positions[i]` (and `y1`/`z1`) as `TS7022` (implicit circular `any`). Added explicit `: number` annotations. Harmless under TS6.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| TS6 `tsc -b tsconfig.devpackages.json` | ✅ 0 errors |
| TS7 `tsgo -b tsconfig.devpackages.json` | ✅ 0 errors |
| TS7 config load (`baseUrl` TS5102 / TS5090) | ✅ resolved |
| `npm run test:unit` (vitest) | ✅ 252 files, 4192 pass, 1 expected-fail, 30 skipped |
| prettier + eslint on changed files | ✅ clean |

Verified against `@typescript/native-preview@7.0.0-dev` and `typescript@7.0.2` (identical results — the `typescript@7` package delegates to the native binary).

## Scope / not in this PR

- The pinned `typescript` devDependency is intentionally left at `~6.0.2`. TS7 is not yet stable, and this PR only removes the barriers so the repo *can* build under it. Bumping the compiler is a separate step for when TS7 stabilizes.
- The whole-repo `tsconfig.test.json` compile still reports pre-existing errors (public `@babylonjs/*` package tests needing built packages, generated smart-filter files). These are **identical on TS6 and TS7 before and after this change** — not introduced here and not a real compile target.

body:
## Summary

GLM-4.7-generation models (`glm4_moe`, `glm4_moe_lite`, `glm_moe_dsa`, `glm4v_moe`) and LongCat-Flash emit tool calls in an XML-ish key/value grammar (`NAME<arg_key>K</arg_key><arg_value>V</arg_value>`) that `src/server/tool_calls/formats.rs` could not parse, so tools requests against these families returned plain text instead of structured `tool_calls`. The two grammars are byte-for-byte identical apart from tag names, so both are implemented over one shared driver.

## What changed

- `formats.rs`: new shared `try_kv_grammar` driver parameterised by a `KvGrammarTags` set, plus `try_glm47` / `try_longcat`. The primary grammar takes the function name as all text before the first `<arg_key>` and each `<arg_key>K</arg_key>` (optional whitespace) `<arg_value>V</arg_value>` pair as an argument. Value coercion is schema-aware: a `string`-typed parameter keeps its raw text, any other type is JSON-parsed then loose-literal parsed then left raw. This reuses the existing MiniMax M3 schema-type mapper (`minimax_m3_schema_type`) and fallback coercion (`minimax_m3_fallback_coerce`) rather than adding parallel helpers. Defensive fallbacks (JSON tool object in `{name, arguments}` / `{function, arguments}` / `{tool: {...}}` shapes, `NAME {json}` / `NAME\n{json}`, and `NAME key=value` shell-style split) fire only when no `<arg_key>` is present and require a plausible bare identifier as the name so other `<tool_call>`-wrapped formats are not misclaimed.
- `types.rs`: `ToolCallFormat::{Glm47, Longcat}`.
- `parser.rs`: `try_glm47` and `try_longcat` run as pre-loop calls (like `try_minimax_m3`) because they need the request tool schema, ordered ahead of the `try_hermes` marker loop. GLM shares the `<tool_call>` block tags with Hermes, so `try_glm47` declines cleanly on a bare `{name, arguments}` JSON body and falls through to `try_hermes`; the non-JSON key/value grammar is claimed before Hermes sees it.
- `stream_filter.rs`: `<longcat_tool_call>` / `</longcat_tool_call>` enter/exit rows added to `CHAT_DELIMITERS` (GLM reuses the existing `<tool_call>` rows). The tags do not prefix- or substring-collide with any existing entry and stay under the current longest delimiter, so the partial-match window is unchanged.

## Ordering / no-misrouting proof

- A genuine Hermes `<tool_call>{json}</tool_call>` still routes to `try_hermes` (format `Hermes`), never GLM: `parse_hermes_json_body_routes_to_hermes_not_glm47`.
- A wrapped Qwen3-Coder `<tool_call><function=...>` still routes to Qwen3-Coder: `parse_glm47_does_not_regress_qwen3_coder`.
- A bare JSON `{name, arguments}` object is not claimed by GLM: `parse_glm47_does_not_regress_generic_json`.
- The GLM primary grammar's non-JSON body is claimed as GLM before Hermes: `parse_glm47_primary_end_to_end`.

## Test plan

Validated on GB10 (CUDA backend, release profile). 301 `server::tool_calls` tests pass, including 33 new tests:

- [x] `cargo test --release --lib server::tool_calls --features cuda` — 301 passed, 0 failed
- [x] GLM/LongCat unit tests: single/multiple args, multiline values, string-typed vs numeric-typed coercion, no-schema loose coercion, each fallback shape (JSON `{function}`/`{tool}`, `NAME {json}`, `NAME\n{json}`, shell `key=value` incl. quoted), parallel calls, malformed-returns-None
- [x] Streaming: `longcat_tool_call_suppressed_single_feed`, `longcat_content_before_block_emitted`, `longcat_streaming_split_at_every_byte_boundary`
- [x] Existing hermes/qwen3_coder/generic_json ordering tests stay green
- [x] `cargo clippy --release -p mlxcel --lib --tests --features cuda --no-deps -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean

Closes #765

body:
## Spec-to-Reconciliation — Phase 3 (Developer Handoff + Submissions)

Builds on the specification-versioning foundation (#465). Adds the next two **child resources of the Work Item root** — the bridge between an approved spec and the reconciliation that will verify it. The Work Item stays the permanent root; `work-items.router.ts` is untouched.

### `DevelopmentTarget` — the developer handoff (spec §5)
One per Work Item. Takes the **active APPROVED** specification version and makes it developer-ready.

| Route | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `GET /development-target` | current handoff + active approved spec pointer |
| `PUT /development-target` | validates requirement scope + required-evidence against the approved spec; returns the target to **DRAFT** |
| `POST /development-target/publish` | re-checks the spec is still APPROVED; emits `DEVELOPER_PACKAGE_PUBLISHED` |
| `GET /developer-package` | read-only: spec summary + scope + base commit + a **pre-filled submission manifest template** |

### `ImplementationSubmission` — one immutable attempt per head SHA (spec §7)
Registering the same `(repository, headCommit)` twice returns the existing record (**idempotent webhooks**), never rewriting history.

A pure, deterministic validator (`submission.validator.ts`, unit-tested) is the **identity gate**:
- **Errors** (recorded as `REJECTED`, never dropped): `spec-hash-matches`, `repository-matches`, `claims-reference-in-scope`
- **Warnings** (non-blocking): unclaimed requirements, missing evidence, unexplained skips, a rebased base commit

Claims remain *declarations* — reconciliation (next phase) independently verifies them.

### Data model (M87)
`development_targets` + `implementation_submissions`, both with FK + cascade from `work_items`; submissions also FK to `specification_versions`. Every action writes to the **Work Item event timeline** via the existing audit path. **No new event-enum members** — M86 (#465) already added `DEVELOPER_PACKAGE_PUBLISHED` / `IMPLEMENTATION_SUBMITTED`.

### Verification
- `prisma validate` + `generate` clean
- workgraph-api `tsc --noEmit` clean
- submissions + specifications suites **12/12** green (pure schema/validator coverage)
- DB-backed service + M87 migration run on a live stack (CI dormant since 2026-06-09)

### Phased roadmap
1. ✅ Spec versioning backend — #465
2. ✅ **Developer handoff + submissions — this PR**
3. ⏭️ Deterministic reconciliation (`ReconciliationRun`/`RequirementVerdict`, reusing `DIFF_VS_DESIGN` + the Governance Gate + the `PendingExecution` runner queue) + GitHub webhook intake
4. ⏭️ Tabbed Work Item workspace frontend (Overview / Specification / Submissions / Reconciliation)

author: korjavin
body:
Closes bd med-yor.15.

## Problem
No cloud auth ceremony had a per-IP rate limiter. `newRateLimiter`/`rateLimiter` were used only by `mcp_endpoint.go`, `mcp_relay.go`, and `trial_proxy.go`. The WebAuthn register/login/reauth ceremonies had zero rate-limit references; claim-token consumption (inside the register ceremony) had only a constant-time compare; `/api/recover` had only a per-account DB throttle (5/hr). An attacker could brute-force claim/recovery/login from a single IP unthrottled.

## Fix
Reuse the existing in-memory `rateLimiter` (no new limiter type) on:
- `POST /api/webauthn/register/begin|finish` (also carry the signup-claim + device-enrollment tokens)
- `POST /api/webauthn/login/begin|finish`
- `POST /api/account/reauth` (additive to its existing session gate)
- `POST /api/recover` (additive to the existing per-account DB throttle)

Generous ceiling: **30/min/IP** — human-paced ceremonies, so multi-device households never trip it.

## Traefik regression guard (the critical part)
Behind Traefik every request shares the proxy's `RemoteAddr`. Keying on `RemoteAddr` would create **one global bucket** and rate-limit every user's login at once (an outage). New `clientIP()` keys on the **last `X-Forwarded-For` hop** (the address Traefik appends, which a client-supplied header cannot spoof), falling back to `X-Real-IP` then `RemoteAddr`. A test asserts two distinct forwarded IPs get independent buckets.

## No enumeration oracle
The 429 is a bare `http.Error(..., "Too Many Requests")` — identical for every caller regardless of account/credential/claim existence, preserving the deliberately-uniform unauthenticated error surface.

## Tests (new `rate_limit_test.go`)
- `TestClientIP` — XFF last-hop, X-Real-IP fallback, RemoteAddr fallback, precedence (Traefik regression guard).
- `TestLimitByIP` — limit trip, window reset, **distinct-IP independence**, generic-body no-leak assertion.
- `TestWebAuthnRoutes_PerIPRateLimited` — end-to-end wiring proof through the real mux, per-IP keying holds.

## Verification
`go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/cloudserver/...`, and `go test ./internal/cloudserver/...` all green.

## Describe Your Changes

### 1. **Fix: Stop Generation Without Unloading Model** (#8426)
**Commit**: `313c65bd1`

**Problem**: Pressing stop escalated to force-unload, evicting the model from VRAM and discarding its KV cache. Resending then forced a full model reload + prompt re-ingestion instead of reusing the cached prefix.

**Root cause**: `tauri-plugin-http 2.5.2`'s `fetch_read_body` drained response bodies with no cancellation support. Aborting the HTTP request didn't stop the connection—the router never saw client disconnect.

**Solution**:
- Bump `tauri-plugin-http` to 2.5.9 (JS + Rust), which reads body chunk-by-chunk and calls `fetch_cancel_body` on abort
- Router observes disconnect and stops generation with model loaded + KV cache intact
- Remove the now-dead `force_stop_model` Tauri command
- Remove escalation logic from `ChatInput.tsx` (also violated guest-js invoke rule)
- Tauri stack upgraded to 2.10.3 (resolves RUSTSEC-2026-0009, no new advisories)

**Files changed**:
- `web-app/src/containers/ChatInput.tsx` — remove force_stop_model escalation
- `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` — bump tauri-plugin-http
- `src-tauri/plugins/tauri-plugin-llamacpp/src/commands.rs` — remove force_stop_model command

### 2. **Feature: Auto-Generate Title Setting + Backend Settings Storage**
**Commit**: `a79f753f3`

**Problem**: 
- No user control over title generation (always on)

- New `backend-settings.ts` helper routes all persistence through `settings_get/set/remove` Tauri commands

---

### 3. **Fix: Thread Reasoning Rail Through Tool Calls**
**Commit**: `d51dd582b`

**Problem**:
- Reasoning trace restarted when a tool call appeared between paragraphs
- "Fold interim text into reasoning" setting added complexity for limited benefit

**Solution**:
- Render finished reasoning as one continuous dotted rail
- Tool calls between reasoning steps stay threaded without restarting rail

---

### 4. **Feature: Unified Logging**
**Commit**: `68b02f816`

**Problem**: Inconsistent logging across web-app, core, and extensions—mix of console.*, tauri-plugin-log direct calls, and no single app.log path.

**Solution**:
- New shared `logger` in `@janhq/core` (levels → console.*, no Tauri dependency)
- Web-app console interceptor in `main.tsx` forwards console.* → app.log via tauri-plugin-log
  - Release builds: warn/error/info
  - Debug builds: also debug/log
- Reuses core's `formatLogArg` utility
- Migrate all extensions + core to shared logger
- Drop direct `@tauri-apps/plugin-log` usage (fixes double-logging now interceptor forwards console.*)

- `extensions/llamacpp-extension/src/test/util.test.ts` — add logger to mocks

---

### 5. **Fix: MLX Server Swift Jinja Pinning**
**Commit**: `a5d1ea6f9`

**Problem**: CI drifted onto `swift-jinja 2.4.0`, which changed `Value.object` keys from `String` → `ObjectKey`, breaking compilation against `swift-transformers 1.3.3`.

**Solution**: Constrain `swift-jinja` to `<2.4.0` in `mlx-server/Package.swift`.

### 6. **Fix: Restore Anthropic and OpenAI Providers** (SSE + Thinking Regressions)
**Commit**: `53dc64e05`

**Problems**:
1. SSE frame filter was applied unconditionally, deleting all named events (Anthropic + OpenAI Responses API use named-only frames) → empty messages
2. Anthropic thinking support didn't account for model generation capabilities
3. Empty API key fell back to empty auth header → misleading 401 error

**Solutions**:
- `filterDefaultSseEvents` → `filterNamedSseEvents` (opt-in, enabled only for llamacpp/MLX/openai-compatible)

  - 4.6+ adaptive, 4.7+ with display

- `web-app/src/lib/model-factory.ts` — gate Anthropic thinking by model generation, opt-in SSE filter
- `web-app/src/lib/reasoningProviderOptions.ts` — Anthropic thinking logic
- Tests updated (`model-factory.test.ts`, `reasoningProviderOptions.test.ts`)

---

### 7. **Fix: Thread List Fetch Failures**
**Commit**: `789731043`

**Problem**: `listThreads()` swallowed errors into `[]`, and race conditions could overwrite a populated list with empty results.

**Solution**:
- Let failures propagate so retry loop kicks in
- Skip empty-result overwrites when threads already loaded
- Re-arm fetch on late extension registration
- Backoff + retry logic ensures eventual consistency

**Files changed**:
- `web-app/src/services/threads/default.ts` — fix error handling + empty-result guard
- `web-app/src/routes/threads/$threadId.tsx` — skip empty overwrites
- Tests updated (`threads.test.ts`)

---

body:
## What & why

`invoices.js` and `location_dialog.js` already ignore a re-entrant submit while a write is in flight, but the **stock** and **New Type** forms in `app.js` and the **New Component** dialog did not — a fast double-click could POST twice (duplicate stock movement / component / type). This brings the remaining write handlers in line.

## Changes

- **`app.js`** — a `makeGuard()` factory gives the stock form and the New Type form **each their own** in-flight flag. They're independent dialogs, so a single shared flag would let one form's in-flight write (or its post-success `loadTable()`) silently swallow the other form's submit.
- **`component_dialog.js`** — an inline `submitting` guard around the create submit, plus wrapping `onCreated` in try/catch so a caller's DOM hook can't surface as an unhandled rejection after the component is already persisted (mirrors `location_dialog.js`).

## Tests

- Each form ignores a second submit while its POST is in flight (exactly one request) — stock, New Type, New Component.
- The stock guard is released after the "choose a location" validation error, so a corrected resubmit posts.
- An in-flight stock POST does **not** block a New Type submit (proves the per-form guards are separate).

A critical review flagged the original shared-flag version as a regression (one dialog's in-flight write swallowing the other's submit) and an inconsistent `onCreated` error path — both addressed here (per-form guards + try/catch), with the isolation and validation-release tests added.

## What changed

- replaced the Phone Pad's unbounded pairing attempt with stage-specific library, signaling, and direct-link timeouts
- made every manual retry cancel the exact stale PeerJS session before opening a fresh one
- added two bounded automatic retries, stale-callback guards, disconnect handling, and a stability window that prevents reconnect loops
- added laptop-side pending-connection timeouts, safe teardown, pairing-code refresh, and reusable codes after a phone disconnects
- added jsDelivr-to-esm.sh fallback loading for PeerJS and QR generation
- added an accessible phone pairing progress card with actionable errors and accurate internet/WebRTC guidance
- guarded wake-lock resolution and restored pairing correctly after browser back/forward-cache returns
- bumped the service-worker cache and updated troubleshooting documentation

## Why

The QR link auto-started `connect()`, set `connecting = true`, and could wait forever without a signaling or data-channel timeout. Because the Connect handler returned while that flag was set, tapping Connect did nothing and the phone remained on “Finding laptop…”. The laptop had the same missing pending-connection cleanup and could retain stale PeerJS state.

Same Wi-Fi also was described as though it performed discovery. Pairing actually needs internet access to PeerJS Cloud before the encrypted WebRTC data channel opens, and restrictive VPN/firewall/guest-network policies can still block that direct route.

## Impact

Successful Phone Pad sessions still use the existing data-only WebRTC protocol. Failed sessions now recover or stop with a useful explanation and an active Try again action instead of hanging indefinitely. Users can refresh a laptop pairing code without closing the dialog, and a blocked primary CDN no longer prevents the feature from loading.

﻿# Add configurable input mapping UI

## Summary
Add a configurable Input Mapping dialog for keyboard, mouse, and external controller input. Pad reads now pass through a saved input profile that the user can edit at runtime; keyboard/mouse bindings are layered under whatever physical pad (DualSense *or* Xbox/XInput) is connected.

The profile lives per-user (`%APPDATA%\SharpEmu\pad-input-profile.json` on Windows, `~/.config/SharpEmu/pad-input-profile.json` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/SharpEmu/pad-input-profile.json` on macOS), not next to the emulator executable — switched per the maintainer's review.

## What changed

### New files
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/SharpEmu.GUI/InputMappingWindow.axaml` | The mapping dialog. Uses the shared design language (`Border.card`, `TextBlock.sectionTitle`, `Button.ghost`/`accent`, `Border.mappingRow`); the per-button callout styling (`mapHotspot`) is window-local because it has to sit over the controller art. |
| `src/SharpEmu.GUI/InputMappingWindow.axaml.cs` | Code-behind. Every visible string is sourced through the localization system. |
| `src/SharpEmu.Libs/Pad/PadInputProfile.cs` | Profile data model + enums (`PadLogicalControl`, `PadStickSource`, `PadStickSide`, `PadInputBindingKind`) + `CreateDefault()` factory (WASD/IJKL/Z/X/C/V/Q/E/R/F/Tab defaults). |
| `src/SharpEmu.Libs/Pad/PadInputProfileStore.cs` | On-disk persistence. **Saves under the OS user directory** (see comment at line 24-25). Re-reads only when the file mtime changes, so live edits in the GUI take effect on the next `scePadRead` without an emulator restart. |
| `src/SharpEmu.Libs/Pad/PadMappedInputReader.cs` | Reads keyboard/mouse bindings out of the profile into a `PadState`. Already honours "only sample the keyboard while the emulator window is focused" (via `PlatformPadInputSource.IsInputActive`). |
| `src/SharpEmu.Libs/Pad/PlatformPadInputSource.cs` | Platform abstraction: `IsInputActive` (window-focus gate) + `IsBindingDown` + `ReadMouseDelta`. Windows implementation uses `GetAsyncKeyState`/`GetForegroundWindow`/`GetCursorPos`; non-Windows uses a Null source (input disabled), keeping the build portable. |

| `LICENSES/LicenseRef-Vecteezy-Free-License.txt` | The Vecteezy license text — REUSE requires this file because the asset uses a custom `LicenseRef-` identifier (REUSE would otherwise report `MissingLicense`). |

### Modified files
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/SharpEmu.Libs/Pad/PadExports.cs` | `WriteNeutralPadData` now reads keyboard/mouse via `PadMappedInputReader.Read(profile)` and merges DualSense + XInput on top (when `EnableExternalController` is set). Both pads contribute when both are plugged in; the controller's axis wins past a 10-unit deadzone. The boot-time controls announcement uses upstream #189's `Interlocked.Exchange` one-shot guard, with this PR's profile-aware `DescribeControls(profile)` message inside (so the printed hint reflects the user's actual saved mappings rather than hardcoded WASD/IJKL defaults). |
| `src/SharpEmu.GUI/MainWindow.axaml` | Added one row to the Options → LAUNCHER card: "Input mapping / Open…" (matches the "Log file path" row pattern). The launch bar itself is unchanged. |

| `src/SharpEmu.GUI/App.axaml` | Lifted the mapping row style into the shared vocabulary as `Border.mappingRow` (`ElevatedBrush` bg, corner 8, padding `10,8`) so the dialog rows match the rest of the UI. |
| `src/SharpEmu.GUI/SharpEmu.GUI.csproj` | Compiles the six `Pad/*.cs` files directly into the GUI (linked), so the launcher doesn't pull all of `SharpEmu.Libs`. Adds the Vecteezy image as an `AvaloniaResource`. |
| `src/SharpEmu.GUI/Languages/en.json` | Added 53 keys: 3 in `Options.InputMapping.*` and 50 in the `Input.*` namespace. Total now 171 (upstream added another 16 `Env.*`/`About.*` between earlier iterations of this PR — those are upstream's, not mine). |
| `src/SharpEmu.GUI/Languages/tr.json` | Same 53 input-related keys added (Turkish). Total now 155. The 16 upstream `Env.*`/`About.*` keys the upstream PRs added to `en` but not to `tr` fall back to English via `Localization._fallbackStrings`, same as before this PR. |
| `REUSE.toml` | Declares the Vecteezy assets with `SPDX-License-Identifier = "LicenseRef-Vecteezy-Free-License"` so `reuse lint` is happy. |

### Removed files
| File | Reason |
|---|---|
| `assets/images/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` | Redundant with REUSE — the Vecteezy asset licensing is fully documented in `REUSE.toml` + `LICENSES/LicenseRef-Vecteezy-Free-License.txt` already. Per the maintainer's review. |

---

## What didn't change — and why

### Xbox controller art / labels in the Input Mapping window
**Status:** open.

The DualSense-only art and PlayStation-shaped callout labels (Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle, L1/R1/L2/R2, TouchPad/Options) are still in place. A user on an Xbox controller who opens the mapping window still sees DualSense labels.

Reason I haven't touched it: **at the input-source level, Xbox already works** — `XInputReader.Translate` (`XInputReader.cs:178-211`) maps A/B/X/Y, LB/RB/LT/RT, Menu/View, and the D-pad into the same ORBIS pad flags DualSense uses, and `WriteNeutralPadData` merges both XInput and DualSense state every frame, so an Xbox Series / Xbox 360 (or any XInput-compatible) controller drives in-game input with zero configuration. An Xbox user with a working controller has nothing to remap.

Given that, it's not clear which behaviour the maintainer wants:
1. **Dynamic relabel** — when an Xbox pad is detected, swap callouts to A/B/X/Y + LB/RB/LT/RT + Menu/View. No art change.
2. **Art swap** — find a properly-licensed Xbox controller illustration and switch art based on the active pad (adds a third-party asset; needs its own REUSE entry).
3. **Dual labels** — render "Cross / A", "L1 / LB", "Options / Menu" on every callout. No art change, no detection needed.
4. **Decouple** — treat the mapping window as keyboard/mouse-only and drop the controller illustration entirely.

This PR does the smallest correct thing the maintainer explicitly asked for ("save the JSON under the users directory instead") and leaves the labelling question open for a follow-up.

**Status:** intentionally not done.

12 other language files exist now (`ar`, `br`, `de`, `dk`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, `ja`, `ko`, `nl`, `ru` + my `tr`). I only added the 53 new keys to `en` and `tr` (the languages I work in). ## Summary

- force OpenRouter DeepSeek requests with one required tool to name that function explicitly
- remove duplicate assistant progress turns and sanitize legacy histories that DeepSeek rejects as prefixes
- make repeated-tool completion decisions assess missing work before selecting the final action

DeepSeek could reject a tool-enabled continuation when a non-blocking progress message was recorded both as a tool result and as a trailing assistant prefix. author: chrisrackauckas-claude
body:
Please ignore this PR until reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas.

## Summary

- Replace exact equality for a sum of three reconstructed magnetic-flux observables with an absolute four-ULP bound derived from their simulated scale.
- Keep the test sensitive to physical flux-balance regressions without assuming that reconstructed `Float64` observables cancel bit-for-bit after two additions.

## Root cause and boundary

The connector equation remains symbolically exact, but ModelingToolkit's perfect-alias elimination changes which fluxes are solved directly and which are reconstructed as observables. The queried `Float64` values therefore accumulate reconstruction and summation roundoff even though the physical balance is unchanged.

The release boundary is ModelingToolkit 11.19 (passes) to 11.20 (fails). Companion-only controls pass with MTK 11.19 + MTKBase 1.29.1 and with MTK 11.19 + MTKTearing 1.12.1. On an otherwise identical Julia 1.12.6 / MTKBase 1.29.1 / MTKTearing 1.12.1 stack:

- `a4bf0bd37e`, the parent of the alias-elimination change: 3/3 pass.
- `c49d619f6c` (`feat: eliminate perfect aliases in favor of higher priority variables`): 2/3, failing only the exact flux-balance equality.

Older boundary checks also pass with MTKSL 2.21.1 / MTK 9.84, MTKSL 2.22.0 / MTK 10.32, and current MTKSL source with MTK 11.0, 11.15, 11.18, and 11.19. MTK 11.20 and current MTK 11.31 reproduce the one-ULP residual.

The observed maximum residual is `2.168404344971009e-19`, exactly `eps(flux_scale)`, at a maximum flux scale of about `1.72464e-3`. It is unchanged with `abstol = reltol = 1e-12` and across Julia 1.10, 1.12, and 1.13 RC. The new ceiling is `4 * eps(flux_scale)`, an absolute-only bound of about `8.67e-19` that covers three reconstructed values and two additions while remaining sensitive at roughly `5e-16` relative to the flux scale.

## Validation

- Julia 1.10.11 focused `test/magnetic.jl`: 3/3 pass.
- Julia 1.12.6 focused `test/magnetic.jl`: 3/3 pass.
- Julia 1.13.0-rc1 focused `test/magnetic.jl`: 3/3 pass (after pre-existing stdlib package-image warnings).

## Summary

- add a typed module-only import-binding fact to the frontend statement model
- let binding layout, early-error validation, and hoisting consume import bindings directly as lexical declarations
- omit import bindings structurally from executable declaration bytecode
- delete `compile_module_program`, its import-name `BTreeSet`, and the cloned top-level executable statement list
- preserve module live bindings, TDZ, and lexical conflict behavior

## Motivation

The audit found that imports masqueraded as otherwise-illegal initializer-less `const` declarations. Module compilation then recognized and removed them by matching declaration shape plus source-name membership, while layout and hoisting deliberately consumed the same forged statements. That load-bearing convention could silently execute an import as a declaration after a frontend refactor.

## Noteworthy decisions

- Import bindings remain lexical and uninitialized until runtime dependency linking, matching their existing semantics.
- Scripts, eval, and modules now share the same bytecode compiler entrypoint; only the typed statement behavior differs.
- The architecture inventory records the semantic boundary and explicitly allows the concrete frontend node, cell, and alias representations to change.
- No source-spelling or enum-shape architecture guard was added; behavior and typed exhaustive matching are the evidence.

author: kupdriveouter
body:
The alignment had a circular problem at its heart, and the screen was on the wrong side of it.

It opened with a list of star names, each annotated `SW, 45 deg` — which is precisely what a beginner **cannot use**, because knowing where south-west *is* requires the compass that this step exists to produce. Until you align, you have no directions. The screen was answering *"where is it?"* when it needed to answer *"what does it look like?"*.

## The Moon is the way out of the loop

It needs no direction and no sky knowledge. You look at it. So it leads the list whenever it is up, and the ordering is now by how easy something is to **find**, not by how bright it is — Sirius is dazzling and still no help to someone who cannot tell it from a planet.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Moon** | "You cannot miss it. Look at it." |
| **Planets** | "A steady light — it does not twinkle." |
| **Stars** | "A star. It twinkles." |

Steady-vs-twinkling is the one test a beginner can actually apply, standing in a field, with no chart.

Direction is still there but demoted and hedged — *"if you know your bearings"* — and altitude is given in **fists at arm's length**, which is how people are actually taught to measure the sky.

## Two things fall out of taking the beginner seriously

**On a moonless night the screen used to leave them stranded.** It now says when the Moon comes up — *"around 06:13 — much easier"* — which is a real answer and one line of ephemeris. Cross-checked against astropy: it agrees to the minute.

**It will only call a star "the brightest in the sky" when that is unambiguous** — at least half a magnitude clear of the runner-up. Tonight Arcturus and Vega are within 0.05 mag of each other, so it says nothing. Sending someone to find "the brightest star" when two of them look identical is worse than saying nothing at all.

## Also

`Align on a star` → **`Set north`**. Nobody was going to attempt a step that sounded like it required knowing a star.

18 tests green. Verified on the glasses.

## Summary

Part of the `APISIMP-*` epoch-ms → ISO 8601 campaign.

`ProvenanceStatsIO.sinceMillis` and `untilMillis` were `long` epoch-ms window-echo fields on `GET /v2/provenance/stats`. These are timestamp echoes (the effective query window bounds), not durations — inconsistent with the ISO 8601 campaign.

body:
## What changed

The initial sync of a large zone was one silent operation: no progress, no resume after a drop.

- **Seam**: `zoneChanges` gained `resultsLimit: Int?` — a bounded pass returns a single batch with an intermediate token (`fetchAllChanges = false` + `ZoneConfiguration.resultsLimit` on the wire); nil is the previous full pass. The old signatures remain convenience wrappers. The double paginates its coalesced feed by sequence just like the server.
- **Store**: `zoneChanges(since:batchSize:projecting:)` — an `AsyncThrowingStream<ZoneDelta>`: each batch carries its own token; apply and persist as you go — a killed sync resumes from the last applied batch, not from zero. A drained feed finishes the stream.
- **Coordinator**: `batchSize:` and `onProgress:` in init — the token advances/persists and live queries tick per batch; progress is a running count of changes (the feed total is unknown up front, so a count, not a fraction). Externally it still returns one aggregate delta.

## Tests

`batchedZoneSync` (batches [2,2,1], resume from the first batch's token, drained feed), `batchedCoordinator` (progress [2,4,5], next pass empty) + the contract test `batchedZoneChanges`. 296 local tests green, lint clean. **Live run against real CloudKit: 23/23 green.**

author: jwarykowski
body:
## Problem

The header's \`● unsaved\` / \`● saved\` indicator is driven by a bare \`dirty bool\`. Every mutation sets it true; save clears it. But undo (\`U\`) and redo (\`ctrl+r\`) **unconditionally** set \`dirty = true\`, so undoing an edit back to the exact on-disk content still shows \`● unsaved\` — there was no saved baseline to compare against.

## Fix

Track a content **fingerprint of the last-saved board** as the single source of truth; \`dirty\` becomes a cache recomputed once per event in \`Update\` (not per render frame). Saves/reloads set the baseline via \`markSaved\`. Undo/redo no longer force the flag — it's derived.

The fingerprint is order-independent (per-item \`store.Serialize\`, sorted), so switching view (\`v\`, which reorders items) never reads dirty. Bonus: an edit that nets no change (toggle done twice) correctly reads clean.

## Changes

- \`model.go\`: \`saved\` field; \`fingerprint\`/\`markSaved\`/\`refreshDirty\`; baseline set in \`newModel\`/\`loadGlobal\`.
- \`update.go\`: removed scattered \`dirty = true\` (beforeMutate, undo, redo); \`w\`/editor-reload/autosave/external-reload call \`markSaved\`; KeyMsg dispatch recomputes once.
- \`tui_test.go\`: \`TestDirtyUndoRedo\` regression test; baseline added to autosave-test setups.
- Version bump 0.5.0 → 0.5.1.
